why: the first reviewed landing (#3) began here: nothing before it is owed

answers.nothing: I compared assert-test-run, scan-bundle, scan-secrets, seed-auth-personas, ensure-signing-keys, run.ps1, ci.yml and the e2e spec with the commit messages and the Done list, and each does what they say. I could not check the shell, sign-in and page component sources, which were left out of the package.

I checked empty, absent and duplicate inputs in the seed script (pagination, existing accounts), the scan-bundle marker lookup (missing declaration fails), the evaluateReport floor and skip counts, and the signing-key file states (missing or invalid). The branches are handled.

Each error path ends in a stderr message and a non-zero exit: the script main wrappers, the ConfigurationError handling in auth:personas, the failed build in scan-bundle, and the Invoke-Bun exit-code throw in run.ps1. The seed script is idempotent, so a partial run is repaired by running it again.
The signing-key write is atomic (temp file, then rename), run.ps1 rewrites .env.local in a single WriteAllText, and the CI step writes .env.local once; I saw no interleaving writers.
The diff removes no lines. The only modified files (.gitattributes, .gitignore, CLAUDE.md, converse.json) are additions.

I checked the set of test statuses in evaluateReport (failed, skipped, pending, todo, disabled), the CSP relaxations scan-bundle rejects, the four personas, and the allowed APP_ENV values. Each is covered.

The keys the changed code builds are the seed accounts' lower-cased email (matched against existing users), the temp key file name with the pid, the CI concurrency group (ci-ref) and the workflow artifact name. None can collide or drift.
The package has no callers section and LEFT OUT lists none; the scripts and the config module the changed scripts use (getConfig, SERVER_ENV_KEYS, getAdminClient) are called as declared.

I checked the scripts' calls into src/server/lib (getConfig, tryGetConfig, getAdminClient, SERVER_ENV_KEYS) against their shown declarations. The auth admin calls in seed-auth-personas.ts have their error results checked.

The env example files list exactly the config schema keys plus the two VITE_ keys, and the demo account list in seed-auth-personas.ts matches demoAccountList.ts. The changed files store no persisted shape.

The Supabase stack is stopped in ci.yml with `if: always()`, and ensure-signing-keys.mjs writes through a temporary file and a rename. The siblings of seed-auth-personas.ts under scripts/dev are not shown.

I read the added lines against the CLAUDE.md rules. They use bun, bunx and bun <file> rather than npm or node, and process.env is read only in the config module (e2e_tests/playwright.config.ts reads it too, but e2e_tests is outside the lint scope and outside what the rule covers). They add no console.log and no issue numbers in comments, and reports go to test directories that are git-ignored.

I checked the loops in scan-secrets, scan-bundle, assert-test-run and seed-auth-personas. Each loop goes round once per file, rule or user, rules are built once outside the file loop, and the per-match line count in scan-secrets runs only on findings.

I read the added comments in the config files, ci.yml, the scripts, run.ps1 and the env examples. Each one explains a trap, an outside fact or a deliberate choice, and none describes the code as it was before.

I compared the pins and limits against their second declarations. The Bun version 1.4.3 matches in .bun-version and packageManager. The test floors 160 and 63 match the text in the testing doc. The ports 54421 to 54425, 5273, 4273 and 5380 match across the README, CLAUDE.md and the decision log.

I compared the functions in verify.ts, jwks.ts, config, client.ts and hooks.ts with their header comments and the Done list, and each does what is claimed. The tenant-label and accessible-name changes from the second commit are in files whose diffs the package does not show, so I could not check them.

I walked the empty, absent, malformed and wrong-order token inputs in verify.ts, the empty or blank environment values in the config schema, the empty and undefined query values in endpoint.ts, and null requests and 204 responses in client.ts and hooks.ts. All of them are handled.

The only state that outlives a call is the memoized config, JWKS cache, client map, default verifier and API adapters. Each is assigned in a single step and replaced whole, so a reader cannot see a half-written value. The JWKS single-flight guard keeps two refreshes from interleaving.
The diff removes no lines; every file is created.

The unions the code branches on are the allowed algorithms (ES256 and RS256, anything else rejected), the key types EC and RSA, the ApiErrorKind values (the status mapper falls through to 'server'), and the query states loading, error and success. All of them are covered.

The keys built are the Supabase client cache key (url, NUL, key), the JWKS cache key (the JWKS URL) and the query key (endpoint id and user id, the JSON of the request, a reload token and an invalidation version). Each key is distinct per thing it identifies and nothing in it changes while the thing stays the same.

I read the callers shown (useApiQuery and useApiMutation in hooks.ts, useScreenStatus, AuthProvider's configureApiClient, the ApiError consumers, and renderWithProviders). They pass and read the shapes `call`, `ApiError`, `CallOptions` and `ApiClientAdapters` declare, and they handle AbortError and non-ApiError throws.

I checked the callees: `getClaims(token, { jwks })` with its error and null-data results handled, `JwksUnavailableError` caught in the verifier, `getKey` and `refresh`, `installFetch` and `problem`, and the Problem schema. Each is called the way it is declared and its failures are handled.

Problem and FieldError are read only through `Problem.safeParse` in `problemError`, with a fallback when a body does not parse. The `problem()` test helper writes the required fields (type, title, status, correlationId). No stored data is touched.

ALLOWED_JWT_ALGORITHMS and KEY_TYPE_OF cover the same two algorithms, and VerifyFailureReason matches the reasons the verifier returns. The test count of 8 in 03-testing-and-ci.md matches the 8 local-stack tests. The two example env files are not shown, so I could not check them.

I read the added lines against the Stack, Code conventions and Rules sections of CLAUDE.md. `process.env` is read only in config/index.ts, there is no console.log, no `any`, and no TODO or placeholder text. The SPA ESLint config enforces the supabase-js and server import boundaries, and the supabase-js and server restrictions are in place.

The loops in the diff (JWKS key filtering, the header and query builders, the env-file and source scans in tests) each run once per element of a small, bounded input with no repeated reads or parses inside, and the invalidation scan in hooks.ts is capped at 200 entries.

The brand wording, tenant label, the six destinations, the env-key list and the ES256 and local-stack descriptions in CLAUDE.md, README, DD-xx, the docs and the tests agree with each other and with the code shown.

The dependency ranges in src/ui/package.json (react 18 with @types/react 18, zod 4, typescript ~6) agree with the stack named in CLAUDE.md, and the JWKS TTL, stale and timeout defaults are each declared once.

I checked the persona switch and theme actions, the sign-in and session flow, the six-destination registry, the screen states and the sidebar tenant label against the commit messages and the Done list, and found no stated behaviour missing.
I followed rejected API calls, failed supabase sign-in, aborted effects and loader failures; each is caught and normalized to ApiError or a generic result, and no half-done state remains.
The diff only adds files and removes no lines.

I checked the unions the changed code branches on: AuthStatus ('initializing', 'signedOut', 'signedIn'), QueryStatus, the ScreenStatus states and the persona ids. Each is handled in RouteGuard, useApiQuery, ScreenStates and Topbar.

The useApiQuery key is made of endpoint id, user id, JSON of the request, reload token and invalidation version. Two different things cannot collide, and the key only moves when the request, user, reload or invalidation changes. The feature registry dedups by module id, nav id and route path.

I checked the callers of the API client, session slice, feature registry, AuthContext and ScreenStates/QueryView (AppShell, Sidebar, Topbar, UserCard, the six feature pages, main.tsx, the test render helpers). Each gets the arguments and shapes it reads (QueryResult, ScreenStatusResult, FeatureModule, SessionState).

I checked the calls to call(), configureApiClient, Card, Button, ButtonLink, TextField, EmptyState, SkeletonBlock, formatCount, t and the storage helpers. The signatures match, and abort and ApiError rejections are handled in useApiQuery and useScreenStatus.

I checked the Problem schema against problemError in client.ts, the stored ciq.persona and ciq.theme values against readStoredPersona/readStoredTheme (an unknown value is ignored), and DEMO_ACCOUNTS against SEED_ACCOUNTS (a test compares the two). Writers and readers agree.

I compared PERSONA_IDS with the persona options in Topbar and with the `shell.persona.${id}` keys, and the registered nav items with the six destinations. The i18n catalog is not shown, but the registry test asserts every nav label has a translation.

Every effect in the changed code (useApiQuery, useScreenStatus, AuthProvider) returns an abort or unsubscribe cleanup, and configureApiClient and configureScreenLoader return restore functions that the tests call. The failing-path handling in useApiMutation's finally block and the abort guards are correct.

The loops are collectFeatures over the glob result (one entry per feature file), invalidationFor over at most 200 invalidations, the listener loop in invalidateApiQueries, and the chart, nav and persona maps over small fixed lists; none repeats work per item that could be done once outside the loop.

I checked the diff's file headers and the comments beside the changed declarations (hooks.ts, router.tsx, SignInPage, ChartFrame, AuthProvider, session slice); each describes behaviour the code has or records a trap, a deliberate choice or an outside fact.

I compared the facts the change states in several places (tenant label DEMO, the six destinations, persona storage keys, ports, the Bun pin and package-script rules) across CLAUDE.md, the README, the design decisions, the technical docs and the tests; they agree.

I compared the ports (54421 to 54424 in CLAUDE.md and DD-09, plus 5273, 4273 and 5380), the Bun pin in package.json and the docs, and the 200-entry invalidation cap, which has no second declaration; the numbers agree.
I read AppShell, Sidebar, Topbar and UserCard against the Done list (six nav items, persona switch stored via choosePersona, theme toggle, user card) and the shell code does what the commits say.
I checked the empty, absent, zero and edge inputs in the shell and in the DataTable, Pagination, KpiCard and DetailList components, and found no defect I could anchor to a numbered line.
The changed code writes only React state, `localStorage` through choosePersona and chooseTheme (single synchronous writes), and DOM focus; I saw no interleaving or half-written state.
The diff removes no lines; every file is created.
I checked the BannerTone, ChipTone, ButtonVariant and ApiError kind branches (describeError has a default case, ErrorState handles forbidden), and every member is handled.
Keys are nav item id, rowKey, option value and useId-derived ids, all unique within their lists; I found no collision I could anchor to a numbered line.
I checked AppShell's use by buildRoutes (props `modules`), PageHeader's use of PageSlotsContext, and the DataTable, Menu and EmptyState consumers. Props and shapes still match what they read.

I checked the shell's calls to featureRegistry, hooks, personas, sessionActions, tenant, useMediaQuery, focusReturn, format and i18n. Arguments match the declarations, and the ApiError, describeError and formErrors uses in the dialog, table and empty states are consistent.

The persona and theme contract (`ciq.persona`, `ciq.theme`, `isPersonaId` guard) and the FieldError, PageSlots, IconName and ChipTone shapes have matching writers and readers in the code shown. The shell is new in this change, so there is no older stored data to read.
PERSONA_IDS matches the Topbar options and the `shell.persona.*` keys. The six nav destinations match the test list, and MAIN_REGION_ID 'ciq-main' matches the Dialog comment's `#ciq-main`.

I read the added lines against the CLAUDE.md rules: no console.log, no `any`, no raw hex, UI strings go through t(), the SPA does not import server code, and comments carry no issue numbers. I found no breach.

I checked the loops in DataTable (page keys, header and row maps, the isInteractiveTarget ancestor walk), the nav and option maps and the chart/legend maps. Each runs once per row, column or item of a bounded page, and nothing loop-invariant is recomputed inside.

I checked the 768px, six-destination, persona and storage statements in the docs, CLAUDE.md and the code headers against the shown code. They agree, and the wording the change adds is not contradicted elsewhere.

I checked the drawer width (DRAWER_QUERY 767px against the '768px' in the headers), the MAIN_REGION_ID 'ciq-main' against the Dialog header's '#ciq-main', and the sidebar and port notes. They agree. DESIGN TOKENS and the CSS rules are not shown, so nothing further could be compared.
I compared the Menu, Tabs, Dialog-adjacent, ScreenStates and page components with the Done list's loading, empty and error states and the six nav destinations, and found no stated behaviour missing.

I checked the rejected loader in useScreenStatus (converted to an ApiError and retried via reload), the ErrorState and QueryView error paths, and describeError's default branch, and nothing is left half done.
The only writes are component state, a document.title effect, and ToastProvider's id counter and timers; I found no interleaving or partial-write problem.
The diff removes no lines (+2804 -0), so there is nothing to account for.

I checked MenuEntry kinds (action, link, separator, text), StepState, TimelineTone, ToastTone and ApiErrorKind in describeError (the default branch covers unauthenticated and conflict), and each is handled.
The keys are entry.id, tab.id/to, step.id, item.id and `gap-${index}`; they are unique within each list as used, and the useId-derived DOM ids are stable.

I checked the shell callers (UserCard's Menu use, AppShell's pageSlots and focusReturn use, router's SkeletonBlock, the NotFound and RouteError pages' PageHeader use, test render's ToastProvider) against the changed props and exports, and each still gets the shape it reads.

I checked the calls into Card, DetailList, FilterBar, FormFields, format helpers (formatCount, EMPTY_VALUE), Button/IconButton, Dialog and EmptyState/ErrorState/Banner against their declarations, and the arguments match and the error kinds are handled.

ApiError, QueryResult, FieldError, ScreenStatusResult and Catalog are read by errors.ts, formErrors.ts, QueryView, ScreenStates and the feature i18n files in the shape they declare, and no stored shape is involved.

The six feature nav entries (orders 10 to 60, paths and icon names) match the six destinations in the Done list and DD-06, every icon name used exists in ICONS, and the ChipTone and ApiErrorKind lists agree with their users.

I read the added lines against CLAUDE.md (design-system components only, strings through t(), no placeholders, no issue numbers in comments, no console.log, no raw hex) and found no breach; the pages use ScreenStates with t() strings.

The loops are Menu's item queries, Pagination's pageWindow, and the maps over entries, steps, tabs and items. Each runs over a handful of in-memory items, and none repeats a read, parse or search that could be done once before the loop.

ScreenStates and QueryView both draw loading and error states, but they take different inputs (ScreenStatusResult and QueryResult). The diff itself shows no block copied from another file or from further down the same file.

The strings, nav labels, persona and theme wording in the diff agree with the docs and tests shown (DD-06's six destinations and the CLAUDE.md SPA rule). No line under NAMED ELSEWHERE still states a wording the change removed.

The numbers set in the diff are MAX_PAGE_SIZE 100, the default page sizes [10, 25, 50, 100] and DURATION_MS 6000. Each is declared once in the diff, and no second declaration in the package contradicts any of them.

Checked the storage guards, the i18n missing-key fallback, the route error page's chunk and 404 handling, and the format and zonedTime helpers; every failure path is caught or leaves nothing half done.
The only writes are guarded localStorage reads and writes and the module-level i18n maps filled once at load, so nothing is observable half written.
The diff removes no lines (+1480 -0).
The branches on the persona, theme and error kinds (chunk, 404, other) cover every member, and unknown stored values fall back to the defaults.
Checked the formatter cache keyed by timeZone, the catalog keys and the `ciq.` storage keys; each key identifies exactly one thing.

I checked how RouteGuard, router, sessionActions, AuthLayout, Sidebar, UserCard, FooterBar and the feature pages call t, format helpers, storage, LoadingScreen, NotFoundPage and RouteErrorPage, and their arguments and return shapes match.

I checked the configureApiClient, ButtonLink, Button, EmptyState and PageHeader calls in render.tsx, NotFoundPage and RouteErrorPage against their declarations, and the arguments and handling are valid.

I checked the storage keys against DD-07, the isPersonaId guard against PERSONA_IDS, and the SessionState and SessionUser shapes against fixtures.ts. Writers and readers agree, and an unknown stored value falls back to the default.
I checked RESERVED_NAMESPACES against the shell catalog's top-level keys, the shell.persona.* keys against PERSONA_IDS, and the six feature directories against the reserved names. They are in step.
The loops are bounded: formatBytes iterates at most 3 units, the i18n coverage test scans source files once, and the Intl formatters are cached per time zone rather than rebuilt per call.
The shell tenant label, the persona and theme storage keys, and the nav strings agree across the docs, the shell tests and the e2e spec. No place was found that still states the old wording.

The only duplicated number is the drawer breakpoint, which is `767px` in DRAWER_QUERY and in the shell test that reads the same query string. No design tokens are shown, and no version or pin pair is in view that disagrees.

I read the CSP plugin in vite.config.ts, zodConfig.ts, the stylesheet contract tests and the config files against the commit messages and Done list; the shell and sign-in components behind the second commit's claims are not in the diff, so I could not check those claims.

I checked the CSP plugin when index.html lacks the token or VITE_SUPABASE_URL is missing or malformed, the rule() helper in components.test.ts for empty, duplicate and media-query selectors, and the breakpoint boundaries at 1279px and 767px; each behaves as intended.

The change writes only static files plus the transformed index.html string, with no shared state or interleaving writers.
The diff removes no lines (+3270 -0), so nothing is lost.
The unions in the diff are the dev/build CSP branches, the light/dark theme blocks and the three layout tiers (full, rail, drawer); each is covered, including a complete dark token set.
The keys built here are the rolldown chunk-group names and regexes and the rule() selector normalisation; they are distinct and stable, with no collision or drift.

No callers are listed, and the CSS and config files in the diff have no callers; the class names the shown TSX files emit (`ciq-nav-item--active`, `ciq-btn--block`, `ciq-chip--outlined`, `ciq-kpi-value--fit`, `ciq-menu--floating`) all have matching rules in components.css.

The tsconfig `include` and `exclude` lists agree: the root config excludes src/ui and e2e_tests, the node config covers vite.config.ts, and the app config covers src. The ports in config.toml match those in CLAUDE.md and the decision log, and the `--ciq-*` tokens that components.css reads are all defined in tokens.css.

The only lifecycle in this diff is the Vite CSP plugin's `configResolved`/`transformIndexHtml` pair, which keeps a plain flag with nothing to release. The stylesheet's drawer open/closed visibility states are symmetric.

I read the added CSS against the rules: colours, gaps and radii come from `--ciq-*` tokens, and the remaining literal pixel values are widths, heights and font sizes, which the file header allows. There are no issue numbers in comments, no `console.log`, and no `process.env` reads in the shown SPA code.
I compared the added CSS, vite config, tsconfigs and tests against the other files shown and found no logic that duplicates code elsewhere in the package.

I read the header comments and the comments inside the diff (tokens, CSP, zodConfig, config.toml); each records a trap, an outside fact or a deliberate choice, and none claims behaviour the code lacks.
I checked the --tiq to --ciq rename, the ports, the tenant label and the Bun/npm wording across CLAUDE.md, README, the design decisions and the tech docs; they agree, and no stale wording remains.
I compared the breakpoints (1280 and 768), the sidebar and rail widths, the bar-list column and the Supabase ports against tokens.css, the tests and the docs; they are in step.
